answer: One prompt can mint ten thousand ballots, but one quill leaves one fingerprint. Each ballot here must write a fresh 300-word statement — twenty minutes of real handwriting no script can fake — and the network reads its function-word fingerprint: the fifty little words no writer controls. A farm printing 10,000 ballots from one prompt dies by that lantern: any two ballots above 0.90 cosine similarity share one hand, and 9,999 are rejected in a single pass. At 25 cents a word, 10,000 distinct hands cost $750,000 — and the nebula collapses once that light shows one star wearing 10,000 masks.
